transcript.text: Hi everyone. I wanted to get us together to discuss the Customer Programs team's proposed six-week rotation where Lina would serve as acting coordinator. As I understand it, the role would involve about eight hours per week, attending the Tuesday standup, and handling routine escalations independently. Since this is my decision to make, I'd like to follow our normal review process — which means I need to have a check-in with Lina and a current collaborator before I finalize any conditions. I also need to make sure we record a recurring meeting day that Lina can actually attend. So, I'd like to hear from those of you who know more about the specifics. What can you tell me about Lina's situation and how this rotation would work in practice?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share something important about my availability. I have an approved caregiving arrangement that limits my rotation work to exactly 4 hours per week and makes Tuesday mornings unavailable. I didn't raise this with you earlier, Maya, because I assumed the nomination packet already reflected my standard schedule.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I should mention two things I haven't documented yet. First, I've observed that Lina hasn't yet handled a cross-team escalation without help. Second, I already agreed to serve as her escalation mentor for exactly 6 weeks if the rotation is approved. I think both points are relevant to Maya's decision, especially given the expectation that the acting coordinator handle routine escalations independently.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Recurring standup moved to Tuesday afternoon to accommodate caregiving arrangement that makes Tuesday mornings unavailable.
Jordan to serve as Lina's escalation mentor for the full 6-week rotation, with escalations routed through Jordan until Lina demonstrates independent handling capability.
